A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PromptMeta on Nell-One and Wiki-One despite the changed title. Their text, equations and visual material support comparison. v2 ends with references; v4 includes readable Appendices A-C.

before.justification: v2 reports original PromptMeta benchmark results, component ablations and hyperparameter analyses in Tables 2-4.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark and ablation results, semantic-embedding comparisons, a visualization case study and relation-specific results, including Appendix C.

M1.justification: The neighbor aggregation, MSP retrieval and contrastive tuning, fusion MLP, and support/query adaptation procedure are retained. The fusion prompt is renamed a fusion token. BERT/GloVe initialization is evaluated as an embedding configuration; newly documented inverse-relation handling does not establish an underlying algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate few-shot tail-entity prediction on Nell-One and Wiki-One. The added case studies examine relations within these retained benchmarks, without introducing a new domain, population or task requirement.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MetaP for Nell-One 1-shot and RelAdapter for Wiki-One 1-shot and 5-shot. The previous comparator set is retained; other newly discussed methods, such as SAFER, are not evaluated in this comparison.

E3.justification: v4 makes BERT-based semantic embeddings the default instead of GloVe and adds comparisons between these configurations. It also introduces Wiki-One 3-shot ablations and selected-relation case-study protocols. The benchmark splits, candidate sets, metrics and stated training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds a neighbor-aggregation ablation, extends component ablations to Wiki-One, and compares GloVe with BERT. Section 5.7 adds a t-SNE case study, while Appendix C compares semantically related relations against HiRe. These substantially broaden investigation of the proposed mechanisms beyond v2's component ablations and sensitivity tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces GloVe-based PromptMeta results with BERT-based results, including Nell-One 5-shot MRR 0.327 versus 0.338; this is not a same-configuration gain. GANA's reported Nell-One 5-shot MRR changes from 0.295 to 0.245. v4 also adds extensive Wiki-One ablation, embedding-comparison and relation-specific results. The retained GloVe Wiki-One 5-shot Hits@10 changes from 0.473 to 0.472.

T1.justification: Appendix A and Table 5 newly provide component-wise and total asymptotic parameter and multiplication counts, using the assumption K is much smaller than n and d. This is a limited complexity analysis; the central mathematical formulation is retained and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that an MSP pool and learnable fusion combine transferable semantics with relational information to improve few-shot prediction. The claimed benchmark superiority and semantic-embedding resource contribution remain. Renaming few-shot KGC as FSRL and adding supporting case studies do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive limitations concerning semantically related training relations, semantic-embedding quality and memory cost. It introduces interpretations of BERT's contextual advantages and the case studies' semantic geometry. The larger-pool performance decline is now attributed to likely overfitting, extending v2's interpretation in terms of shared semantic patterns.

D1.justification: v4 provides a code/data repository link where v2 promises future release, materially changing the documented access information. It additionally specifies BERT-base-uncased, inverse-relation handling and projection initialization. Appendix B adds baseline links and availability constraints, and changes HiRe's reported provenance from reproduced results to results adopted from its paper.

R1.justification: v4 expands discussion of KG embeddings, including TransR, LASS and KGE-SymCL, and adds SAFER, RelAdapter and related GNN meta-learning literature. It removes the ProG discussion and sharpens distinctions from text-based and GNN-based prompting. The central positioning around underused semantics in few-shot relational prediction remains.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change alongside extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, problem statement and method explanation. Experimental setup and implementation material are reorganized, baseline reproduction discussion moves partly into Appendix B, and new case-study and limitations sections substantially revise the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v4 adds the framework diagram in Figure 1, the t-SNE visualization in Figure 2, and Tables 5-6. Table 3 is redesigned with two dataset panels and separate embedding variants. Table 2 gains comparator rows, bold highlighting and an availability footnote, substantially expanding the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader ablations and embedding comparisons better probe the central semantic-component claim, while clearer exposition, explicit limitations and code/data access information improve assessability. These gains are tempered by new reporting problems: Table 2 gives GANA Wiki-One 5-shot Hits@1 of 0.317 above its MRR of 0.261, and Section 5.5 overstates consistent BERT superiority despite lower Wiki-One 3-shot Hits@5/10 in Table 3. The net improvement is limited.
